'''Aleksandr Mikhailovich Baldin''' (Russian: Александр Михайлович Балдин) (February 26, 1926, Moscow – April 29, 2001) was a Soviet and Russian [[physicist]], expert in the field of physics of elementary particles and [[Particle physics|high energy physics]].

After finishing the railway technical school, he studied in the [[Russian University of Transport|Moscow Institute of Engineers and Transport]], followed by a DSc program in [[National Research Nuclear University MEPhI (Moscow Engineering Physics Institute)|Moscow Engineering Physics Institute]] completing in 1949, when he became a professor in [[Lebedev Physical Institute]]. In 1968, he was named the director of Laboratory of High Energy Physics in the [[Institute for Nuclear Research]] (ОИЯИ) in Dubna, where the Soviet nuclear weapons were developed. He was elected a member of [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] and a faculty of [[Moscow State University]]. He was the co-designer of the project of synchrophasotron ОИЯИ (1949). He received the [[Lenin Prize]] (1988).<ref>{{cite web |url= http://dubna.org/p/?id=19376|title= Балдин Александр Михайлович|author= |date= |publisher= dubna.org |accessdate=2023-01-24 |lang=ru}}</ref>

== Biography ==
He graduated from the railway technical school, and then entered to the [[Russian University of Transport|Moscow State University of Railway Engineering]]. In 1946, as an excellent student, he was invited to continue his studies at the [[National Research Nuclear University MEPhI (Moscow Engineering Physics Institute)|Moscow Engineering Physics Institute]] (MEPI). After graduation in 1949, he was sent to the [[Lebedev Physical Institute]] of the Academy of Sciences of the USSR (PIAS), where he later defended his PhD and became a professor.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.mountain.ru/article/article_display1.php?article_id=6106|title= Балдин Александр Михайлович|author= |date= |publisher= mountain.ru |accessdate=2023-01-24 |lang=ru}}</ref>

In 1952, he became a master of sports in [[mountaineering]] and the champion of the USSR.

He was chairman of the Council on Electromagnetic Interactions of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]], a member of the Bureau of the [[Nuclear physics|Nuclear Physics]] Division of the Russian Academy of Sciences, chief editor of the journal Elementary Particles and Atomic Nuclei (EPAN) and “ Letters to EPAN”, the member of the editorial boards of many scientific publications. He organized several international seminar on High Energy Physics (since 1969).
